name: Villa Auren
description: A contemporary villa shaped by light, honest materials and everyday rituals. Interior concept & investment proposal · September 2026

budget.label: Interior construction & installation
budget.note: Fixed demo package: €28,500 preliminaries/finishes + €18,500 electrical + €14,000 plumbing + €21,000 flooring. All child quotes included.

budget.label: Electrical installation & controls
budget.note: Included in Forma Build. €13,700 installation + €4,800 controls. Decorative fixtures priced separately.

budget.label: Dimming drivers & scene controls
budget.note: Second-tier subquote included in Lumen Works and therefore Forma Build. Do not add again.

budget.label: Plumbing & underfloor heating adaptations
budget.note: Included in Forma Build; excludes sanitary fixtures.

budget.label: Stone floors & mineral wall finishes
budget.note: Included in Forma Build. 150 m² floors and 180 m² wall finishes.

budget.label: Kitchen & fitted oak joinery
budget.note: €26,000 cabinetry + €16,000 stone + €12,000 appliances. Study upgrade excluded.

budget.label: Travertine island & worktops
budget.note: Included in Grain Atelier. Templating, fabrication, delivery and fitting.

budget.label: Integrated appliance package
budget.note: Included in Grain Atelier; induction, extraction, ovens, refrigeration and dishwasher.

budget.label: Optional bespoke study library
budget.note: Additional subquote: not included in the kitchen contract. Off by default; rendered study shows this upgrade.

budget.label: Furniture & rugs selection
budget.note: €36,000 base selection; €44,000 premium upholstery and larger rug specification. Range is a selection allowance, not VAT variation.

budget.label: Decorative lighting
budget.note: Decorative fixtures only; installation and controls are in Forma Build.

budget.label: Curtains & window treatments
budget.note: Measured allowance for 48 linear metres of sheers and bedroom blackout; manual tracks.

budget.label: Bathroom fixtures & vanity
budget.note: Bath, sanitaryware, bronze fittings, vanity and installation of supplied fixtures; rough-in separately included in Flow Systems.

budget.label: Original artwork & styling
budget.note: Two fictional art commissions, framing, ceramics and styling day. AI artwork represents the concept.

budget.label: Interior design & site coordination
budget.note: Concept, design development, procurement coordination and six site visits; excludes structural and permit services.

budget.label: Client-held contingency
budget.note: Uncommitted planning reserve; not a supplier quote or authorisation to spend.

budget.label: Optional terrace furnishing package
budget.note: Loose outdoor furniture and pots only. Exterior landscaping and building works excluded.

budget.label: Landscape design & external works
budget.note: Unpriced and excluded from known total; shown landscape is illustrative.

slides.title: Villa Auren
slides.subtitle: A quieter kind of luxury.
slides.body: A contemporary villa shaped by light, honest materials and everyday rituals. Interior concept & investment proposal · September 2026

slides.title: A home that lets you exhale.
slides.subtitle: 01 / THE STORY
slides.body: For our fictional clients, Eva and Julian Vermeer, home is where busy days become slow evenings. Villa Auren brings the ease of a coastal retreat to a generous modern family house: welcoming, tactile and quietly expressive.
points: Fictional location: Bergen, North Holland
Illustrative whole-villa area: 320 m² over two levels
Detailed design focus: living, dining, kitchen, study and primary suite

slides.title: Beautiful in the everyday.
slides.subtitle: THE CLIENT BRIEF
slides.body: A family home that hosts generously and works effortlessly. Space for cooking together, a place to retreat, and rooms that feel complete without feeling precious.
points: An open social heart with concealed storage
A calm primary suite and a proper place to work
Natural materials with a practical maintenance plan
A transparent investment, with options clearly separated

slides.title: Light. Texture. Restraint.
slides.subtitle: THE DESIGN PRINCIPLES
slides.body: Architecture does the quiet work. A small family of materials flows from room to room; curved furniture softens the long lines, and bronze details give the palette a little depth.
points: Let daylight define the mood
Repeat materials; vary scale and texture
Choose fewer, more generous pieces

slides.title: The architecture is our starting point.
slides.subtitle: CONCEPT CONTEXT
slides.body: The imagined villa has generous glazing, a strong garden connection and a simple two-storey volume. The exterior image establishes the intended atmosphere; it is a generated concept, not a site photograph.
points: No existing-condition survey is represented
Final measurements and services require verification
Garden and architectural shell are outside the interior budget

slides.title: The material language.
slides.subtitle: 02 / EARTH, OAK & STONE
slides.body: M01 limestone · M02 European oak · M03 travertine · M04 ivory mineral finish · M05 brushed bronze. Every selection begins with a physical sample.

slides.title: Softness, with structure.
slides.subtitle: TEXTILE & OBJECT MOODBOARD
slides.body: T01 ivory linen · T02 olive bouclé · T03 mushroom wool · T04 translucent sheers. Earth-toned artwork gives the neutral architecture a warm focal point.

slides.title: A palette borrowed from the dunes.
slides.subtitle: COLOUR & FINISH
slides.body: Chalk and sand make the envelope. Oak brings warmth. Olive grounds the furniture. Bronze adds a quiet, deliberate edge.

slides.title: Connected, never crowded.
slides.subtitle: 03 / SPATIAL STRATEGY
slides.body: Illustrative ground-floor zoning only, not measured or suitable for construction. A clear arrival sequence opens into connected kitchen, dining and living spaces; the study has its own quiet edge. Primary suite is on the upper level.

slides.title: The spaces, together.
slides.subtitle: 3D / SPATIAL STUDY
slides.body: A cutaway model explores the connection between living, dining, kitchen and study. Pale stone and oak hold the rooms together. An illustrative spatial study, not a measured floorplan.

slides.title: The art of staying in.
slides.subtitle: LIVING ROOM
slides.body: A generous curved sofa, olive lounge chairs and a travertine table face the garden. A lower seating zone creates intimacy inside the open room. Any level change remains subject to accessibility and technical review.

slides.title: Shape before atmosphere.
slides.subtitle: 3D / LIVING ROOM MODEL
slides.body: A simple shaded model makes the seating, level change and garden glazing easy to read. Faceted furniture and clear model edges keep the focus on proportion and space.

slides.title: A room made for real life.
slides.subtitle: LIVING / DESIGN NOTES
slides.body: Comfort is designed in: conversational seating, soft acoustic layers, dimmable light and generous space around the central table.
points: Ivory linen sofa with removable cover preference
Olive accent chairs and low-pile wool rug
Original abstract commission in chalk, umber and ochre
Power and lamp positions coordinated before first fix

slides.title: A kitchen with presence.
slides.subtitle: KITCHEN & DINING
slides.body: A sculptural travertine island anchors the room. Flush oak cabinetry conceals the practical things; an oval dining table keeps the transition to the garden relaxed.

slides.title: Everything has its place.
slides.subtitle: KITCHEN / PROCUREMENT
slides.body: The €54,000 kitchen package includes €26,000 of cabinetry and fitting, €16,000 of stone and €12,000 of appliances. Stone and appliance subquotes are included once in that package.
points: Final island dimensions follow measured clearance review
Approve stone slab, edge radius and stain sample
Appliance models agreed before shop drawings
Optional study joinery is a separate €9,600 addition

slides.title: A softer end to the day.
slides.subtitle: PRIMARY BEDROOM
slides.body: A low upholstered bed, oak headboard wall, travertine shelves and layered curtains create an unhurried retreat. The olive accent connects the suite to the rest of the home.

slides.title: A daily ritual, elevated.
slides.subtitle: PRIMARY BATHROOM
slides.body: Travertine, bronze and warm oak carry through to a spa-like bathroom. The €23,500 fixture package is separate from the rough-in plumbing already included in construction.

slides.title: Room to think.
slides.subtitle: STUDY & LIBRARY
slides.body: Garden-facing work space, tactile upholstery and an oak library make this room feel part of the home. The illustrated bespoke library and desk are the optional €9,600 joinery upgrade, unselected in the base budget.

slides.title: An original point of view.
slides.subtitle: ART & OBJECTS
slides.body: “Dune study” — original AI-generated concept artwork for this fictional project. The €6,800 art and styling package allows for two commissions, framing, ceramics and placement. No existing artist is represented.

slides.title: From daylight to lamplight.
slides.subtitle: LIGHTING & ATMOSPHERE
slides.body: Three layers of light allow the architecture to change pace: integrated ambient light, focused task lighting and expressive decorative pieces.
points: Welcome: soft circulation and a warm living-room glow
Gather: dining pendant with kitchen task lighting
Unwind: low-level lamps and bedside reading light
€12,800 decorative supply; wiring and controls included under construction

slides.title: An investment you can follow.
slides.subtitle: 04 / THE BUDGET
slides.body: €278,500–€286,500 including the €25,000 client-held contingency. The range reflects furniture choices. Optional study and terrace packages are off by default. Unpriced landscape works are excluded. All figures are fictional and use an assumed VAT-inclusive basis.

slides.title: One total. Every layer visible.
slides.subtitle: SUPPLIERS & SUB-SUPPLIERS
slides.body: Included subquotes explain a parent price; they do not increase it. The study is an additional optional subquote and increases the total only when selected.

slides.title: Make the choices that matter.
slides.subtitle: OPTIONS & ALLOWANCES
slides.body: Base selection €278,500. Premium furniture adds €8,000; study joinery adds €9,600; terrace furnishings add €18,500. Selecting all three gives €314,600, including contingency and excluding unpriced landscape work.

slides.title: From first sketch to first evening.
slides.subtitle: 05 / THE PROGRAMME
slides.body: An indicative 24-week journey from approved brief. Lead times are fictional planning assumptions and begin after drawings and finishes are approved.

slides.title: Four decisions unlock the next chapter.
slides.subtitle: DESIGN FREEZE
slides.body: A clear approval sequence keeps the project coherent and procurement coordinated.
points: 01 — Approve the spatial concept and material palette
02 — Choose base or premium furniture allowance
03 — Decide on the optional study and terrace packages
04 — Review the scope, exclusions and supplier hierarchy

slides.title: Clarity is part of the design.
slides.subtitle: SCOPE & ASSUMPTIONS
slides.body: The demo budget covers the specified interior packages. It does not price a new villa, architectural shell, structural alterations, professional engineering, permits, landscaping or undisclosed site conditions.
points: All people, suppliers, quotations and prices are fictional
All room images are AI-generated concepts, not completed-work photography
Illustrative VAT assumption: 21% uniformly, for demo arithmetic only
Supplier PDFs, scope notes and budget CSV are included for review

slides.title: Welcome to a slower rhythm.
slides.subtitle: VILLA AUREN
slides.body: A home that feels warm before anyone turns on the lights. Prepared by the fictional Auren Interior Studio for Eva & Julian Vermeer. Demo 01 / Residential villa.
